$comment: Where contracts/lesser/graphql-schema.graphql came from, stated precisely enough
that anyone can re-derive it without trusting this file.
THE TWO PROPERTIES ARE NOT THE SAME PROPERTY, and conflating them is how a pin
starts certifying something it never checked:
INTEGRITY is offline. `sha256` is the digest of the bytes in this repository.
scripts/audit-graphql-documents.mjs recomputes it before it validates anything,
so a schema edited in the same pull request as the documents it is supposed to
judge fails the build. That check proves the bytes have not drifted HERE. It
proves nothing whatsoever about upstream.
PROVENANCE is `blob_sha1`. It is git's own object id for these exact bytes —
sha1('blob ' + length + '\0' + content) — which is the id equaltoai/lesser
itself records for docs/contracts/graphql-schema.graphql at `ref`. Anyone can
check it in one call, against lesser rather than against us:
gh api repos/equaltoai/lesser/contents/docs/contracts/graphql-schema.graphql?ref=<ref> --jq .sha
git hash-object contracts/lesser/graphql-schema.graphql
Both must print blob_sha1. That comparison is the binding to upstream; the
offline digest is not, and this repository never reports a green offline run as
evidence of provenance.
WHY THERE IS NO NETWORK CHECK HERE. A gate that dereferences the pin at build
time is a gate whose answer depends on GitHub being reachable and on the request
being aimed at the right repository — and the aiming is the part an edit loosens.
The M2 predecessor to this file grew four layers of defence around that one
question and still had to be told, by review, that its pin had been able to
choose its own examiner. The honest small version is this: pin the bytes, record
the upstream object id beside them, check integrity offline, and let the
human-verifiable one-liner above be the provenance step.
MOVING THIS PIN is a contract event, not maintenance. Fetch the file at the new
lesser ref, recompute all three values, and re-run the document validation in the
same commit — a schema bump that is not accompanied by a validated document set
is a claim that nothing changed, made without looking.

upstream.ref_description: equaltoai/lesser staging @ 1ce2dc97, the merge of PR #1418 (closes #1417), 2026-08-15. NOT A RELEASE TAG — a staging merge commit, which is what it remains. It was also NOT YET DEPLOYED when this pin was taken; it was deployed on 2026-08-15. See `inspected.forward_pin` for what that state was, and `inspected.forward_pin_resolved` for the record that closed it.

inspected.forward_pin: RESOLVED ON 2026-08-15 — the deploy happened, in the required order; `forward_pin_resolved` below is the record, and is the field to read for current state. WHAT FOLLOWS IS THE HISTORY, kept rather than deleted: it is why the consuming document was written the way it was, and a warning that is simply removed reads afterwards as a warning that was never needed. WHEN THIS PIN WAS TAKEN IT WAS AHEAD OF EVERY DEPLOYED INSTANCE, which no previous pin here had been, so it was stated as a field rather than left in a commit message. Every earlier bump named a published release tag whose contract some instance was already serving; this one named a staging merge commit. `viewerIsOwner` therefore existed in the pinned contract before it existed in any instance's schema, and a GraphQL document selecting it is rejected WHOLE by a server that predates the field — `Cannot query field "viewerIsOwner" on type "Agent"` is a validation error against the document, not a null in the response, so the agent detail read and `myAgents` both fail rather than degrade. contentus took that deliberately (equaltoai/contentus PR #105 for lesser#1417/#1418): the alternative was a second document gated on a guess about the instance's generation, which is the anonymous/owner split `contract.ts` already removed for being an inference where lesser makes a statement. THE ORDERING WAS THEREFORE LOAD-BEARING: lesser staging deploys first, contentus deploys after. Neither the offline integrity check nor the online provenance check could observe that — both compare bytes to a repository, and a repository is not a running instance — so nothing green here ever said the field is served, and nothing green here says it now.
inspected.forward_pin_resolved: THE DEPLOY, recorded by hand because nothing in this repository can record it. On 2026-08-15 the operator deployed lesser at 1ce2dc97 first and contentus at 4d6bb99 after it — the ordering `forward_pin` calls load-bearing, honored in that direction — and browser-verified the `viewerIsOwner`-mounted surfaces live on the dev instance across 2026-08-15/16. The constraint above is SATISFIED, not pending: a reader arriving now should not re-derive a live deploy-ordering rule from it, and nothing in this repository is waiting on a deploy. WHAT THIS FIELD IS AND IS NOT. It is an operator's observation of one instance at one time, transcribed here (equaltoai/contentus issue #106). It is not a gate result, not something either pin check verified, and not a claim about any other instance — neither check gained the ability to see a running server, and both still compare bytes to a repository. A NEW INSTANCE PROVISIONED FROM A LESSER GENERATION OLDER THAN 1ce2dc97 WOULD REOPEN THE SAME QUESTION, and the answer would again have to come from an operator rather than from anything green here.
inspected.corroborating_source: The schema delta from the previous pin (v1.6.5, a1eb3c67) is exactly three added lines, and `git diff` on this artifact shows no others: `Agent.viewerIsOwner: Boolean!` with the docstring 'True when the requesting viewer is this agent's owner under Lesser's canonical local-identity comparison', and a description on the already-present `Query.myAgents` reading 'Agents owned by the viewer. Agents shared with the viewer are served by the shared-with-me index, not this field.' Both match the delta lesser#1418 published for this sync byte for byte. NO FIELD WAS REMOVED, RENAMED OR RETYPED, so nothing contentus already selects is affected. WHAT THE NEW FIELD IS, from lesser's implementation rather than from its name: `applyGraphAgentViewerOwnership` computes it from `auth.AgentOwnerMatchesLocalPrincipal` — the same canonical rule the server already used internally, whose identity comparisons are `strings.EqualFold` (pkg/auth/agent_owner.go), which is why an owner spelled `@Alice`, `ALICE` or `alice` resolves to one answer. It is OWNERSHIP ONLY: lesser deliberately kept `applyGraphAgentViewerState` — ownership plus private-field redaction — as the separate path for the surfaces that depend on visibility semantics, and `viewerIsOwner` is preserved across redaction the way `mcpAccess` is (graph/agent_model_helpers.go), so a non-owner receives it as a served `false` rather than as a redacted blank. Anonymous viewers get `false`. THE CONFLATION THIS RESOLVES is lesser's own note in #1417: `viewerCanSeePrivateFields` answers a VISIBILITY question and is true for owners AND admins, so it was never an ownership statement, and lesser pins the distinction in a contract test (`TestActorAgentInfoAppliesPrivateFieldPolicy` asserts `viewerCanSeePrivateFields=true` with `viewerIsOwner=false` for an admin). contentus consumed the proxy for owner-only mounts from M7 until this sync; that migration ships in the same pull request, which is what makes this bump a consumed contract change rather than a snapshot refresh. Verified against the commit object at 1ce2dc97: `gh api repos/equaltoai/lesser/contents/docs/contracts/graphql-schema.graphql?ref=1ce2dc975bd212c11ffc6b4fca0035bae039bd60 --jq .sha` reports 558c4cf1fbc2d369cc2909786ad50fbe8f68bb58, and `git hash-object` on the bytes in this tree computes the same OID independently.
